title: Data governance terms and how they connect
objective: New team members learn 14 data governance terms in plain English and see which roles, processes and safeguards depend on each other, so the vocabulary reads as one system rather than a list.

recommended.why: A network map puts every term next to the terms it acts on, so the dependencies are visible at a glance, and the focus shows one term with its direct neighbours and their definitions.

alternative.why: A connected map versus a tidy glossary: which helps learners remember how terms relate?

assumptions: Fourteen terms chosen for a first week in a data team; definitions are simplified for newcomers, not legal wording
Three themes: People (roles and the people data is about), Processes (how data is described and kept trustworthy), Safeguards (how data is protected)
Each link reads as a sentence from source to target, for example "Data steward maintains Data catalog"; the 19 links are illustrative, not exhaustive
The focus highlights the chosen term plus every term it shares a link with, in either direction
units: links: count of typed relationships between terms
checkDescription: Every link connects two defined terms, every term has at least one link, and the focus highlights exactly the focus term plus its direct neighbours.
expectAtDefaults: m.focusTerm === 'Access control' && m.terms.filter(t => t.highlighted).length === 5 && m.links.length >= 18 && m.showLabels

learnerPrompts.predict: Before you focus on it: how many terms do you think Access control connects to, and in which themes?
learnerPrompts.explain: Pick a link that crosses from Processes to Safeguards. Say it as a sentence and explain why a privacy team would care about it.
